title: Smart glasses controversy sidelines the benefits for disabled people | Letter

paragraphs.en: Your editorial on Meta’s smart glasses acknowledges their value to blind and visually impaired people, then asks that this “not be allowed to distract” from the harms ( The Guardian view on Meta’s smart glasses: regulators must get on the front foot, 10 August ). As an optometrist who owns a small independent practice, I’d suggest that it is visually impaired people who are being treated as the distraction.
paragraphs.zh: 贵报关于 Meta 智能眼镜的社论承认了它们对盲人和视力障碍者的价值，接着又要求“不得让这分散人们对危害的注意力”（《卫报》观点：Meta 智能眼镜——监管机构必须抢占先机，8 月 10 日）。作为一名经营小型独立诊所的验光师，我想指出，被当作“分散注意力”的恰恰是视力障碍者。

paragraphs.en: I was reluctant to stock Ray‑Ban Meta, having no fondness for Meta or Luxottica, but colleagues persuaded me of the benefits for people with sight impairment. The reality has surpassed that. The majority of our buyers have a visual impairment or learning difficulty. One man, practically illiterate, now has the world read to him.
paragraphs.zh: 我本不愿上架 Ray-Ban Meta，对 Meta 和陆逊梯卡都谈不上好感，但同事们说服了我，说它对视力受损者大有裨益。而实际情况比我预想的还要好。我们大多数购买者都有视力障碍或学习困难。有一位几乎不识字的男士，如今整个世界的文字都有人读给他听了。

paragraphs.en: For many of these patients, leaving the house is already an act of courage. Unfamiliar streets, unreadable signs, the constant low-level anxiety of navigating a world built for the fully sighted. These glasses have quietly made that easier. A week of coverage branding them “pervert glasses” has now added a new anxiety: not whether they can manage the journey, but whether strangers will assume the worst of them for wearing the thing that makes it possible.
paragraphs.zh: 对这些患者中的许多人来说，出门本身就已经是一种勇气的表现。陌生的街道、读不懂的路标、在一个为视力健全者而建的世界里穿行时持续存在的隐隐焦虑。这副眼镜悄无声息地让这一切变得容易了些。而一周来称它们为“变态眼镜”的报道，如今又添了一层新的焦虑：问题不再是他们能否应对这段路程，而是陌生人会不会因为他们戴着这件让这一切成为可能的东西，而对他们做最坏的揣测。

paragraphs.en: A colleague of mine was recently branded a misogynist online, by another optometrist, simply for suggesting the glasses were useful. Opening a Guardian leader with a nickname worthy of a Murdoch red-top – “pervert glasses” – makes that hostility respectable.
paragraphs.zh: 我的一位同事最近仅仅因为说这副眼镜有用，就被另一位验光师在网上打上了厌女者的标签。贵报的社论以配得上默多克旗下小报的绰号——“变态眼镜”——开头，让这种敌意变得体面起来。

paragraphs.en: The harms you describe are real and worth regulating. But on a recent holiday I left my own pair in the hotel room, yet watched hundreds of people photographing poolside on their phones, my daughters frequently in the background, with no permission sought and no bans imposed. The glasses at least announce themselves with a recording light. Pubs, parks and beaches are indeed not film sets, but they have been full of cameras for 20 years. Regulate by all means. Just remember who ends up wearing the stigma. Aled Brassington Romiley, Greater Manchester
paragraphs.zh: 你们所描述的危害是真实的，值得监管。但最近一次度假时，我把自己的那副落在了酒店房间里，却看到数以百计的人用手机对着泳池边拍照，我的女儿们常常出现在背景里，没有人征求同意，也没有任何禁令。这副眼镜至少还有一枚录制指示灯在宣告自己的存在。酒吧、公园和海滩确实不是片场，但二十年来它们早已布满了摄像头。尽管去监管吧。只是请记住，最终背负这层污名的是谁。阿莱德·布拉辛顿，大曼彻斯特罗米利

paragraphs.en: • Much of the coverage of Meta’s smart glasses has been dominated by the language of “spy glasses” and “predator glasses”, while disabled people’s experiences have barely featured. To its credit, your recent report recognised how useful the glasses can be for blind and disabled people ( ‘I’m not spying’: how Meta’s smartglasses have divided opinion, 6 August ). Even so, accessibility still feels like a side issue in the wider debate around smart glasses.
paragraphs.zh: • 围绕 Meta 智能眼镜的报道，大部分都被“间谍眼镜”和“捕食者眼镜”之类的字眼主导，而残障人士的体验几乎未获提及。值得肯定的是，贵报近期的报道（“我不是在偷窥”：Meta 的智能眼镜如何引发分歧，8 月 6 日）承认了这副眼镜对盲人和残障人士多么有用。即便如此，无障碍问题在围绕智能眼镜的更广泛讨论中，仍感觉像是一个边缘议题。

paragraphs.en: I have severe muscular dystrophy and cannot pick up or operate a smartphone. My Ray-Ban Meta glasses let me make calls, send WhatsApp messages, take photos and record moments by voice. I can start a video call without touching a phone. These are not gimmicks. They give me independence and help keep me connected and safe.
paragraphs.zh: 我患有严重的肌营养不良症，无法拿起或操作智能手机。我的 Ray-Ban Meta 眼镜让我可以打电话、发 WhatsApp 消息、拍照，并用语音记录瞬间。我无需触碰手机就能发起视频通话。这些都不是噱头。它们给了我独立自主的能力，帮助我保持联系和安全。

paragraphs.en: I can’t speak for Mark Zuckerberg or defend Meta’s wider record on privacy. But I’ve met Meta developers and scientists working on accessibility. Their commitment is real. They are listening to disabled people and building features that can change lives.
paragraphs.zh: 我不能替马克·扎克伯格说话，也无法为 Meta 在隐私方面的整体纪录辩护。但我见过研究无障碍功能的 Meta 开发者和科学家。他们的投入是真实的。他们在倾听残障人士的声音，并打造能够改变生活的功能。
